detailed_rationale:
Wockhardt is a research-focused pharma company whose reported numbers have been extremely volatile: a Rs 108 Cr loss in the June 2025 quarter was followed by three consecutive profitable quarters (Rs 82 Cr, Rs 61 Cr, and Rs 164 Cr through March 2026), taking FY26 to a full-year turnaround -- Rs 199 Cr net profit and 19% OPM against a Rs 57 Cr loss and 13% OPM in FY25. Revenue grew a respectable 12% YoY to Rs 3,373 Cr. This is a genuine improvement, not an accounting artifact -- margins have expanded every quarter of FY26 and the core formulations/API business appears to be scaling. The company is also known for a long-dated, differentiated pipeline of novel antibiotics targeting drug-resistant gram-negative infections, a program that -- if and when specific molecules clear regulatory milestones and reach the US market -- represents call-option-like upside well beyond the base generics/API business. We could not verify from the sources opened any confirmed near-term (FY27) revenue contribution from that pipeline, so we treat it as unconfirmed optionality rather than a modeled cash flow.

Set against that improvement, three-year average ROE is still just ~6% and ROCE ~8% -- both low in absolute terms and well short of what the current ~120-140x trailing PE implicitly demands. Promoter holding has declined structurally from ~74% (2017) to ~49% today, which is a long multi-year trend (likely capital raises over the cycle) rather than a fresh red flag, but it does mean less promoter skin in the game than a decade ago. Debt is modest and stable (Rs 2,233 Cr, D/E ~0.45x) and interest burden is declining, so balance-sheet risk is not the concern here.

Reverse-DCF read: the market is pricing Wockhardt as if the antibiotic-pipeline optionality is close to being realized at scale. On the demonstrated base business alone -- ~12% revenue growth, margins recovering but still ROE-constrained, one loss-making quarter just 12 months ago -- a 120x+ multiple is not earned yet. We would need to see either the pipeline convert to disclosed, contracted revenue, or several more quarters of the current margin trajectory holding, before treating the valuation as fair rather than rich.
recommendation_rationale: The FY26 turnaround is real and margin-accretive, but three-year ROE (~6%) and ROCE (~8%) remain low, one of the last four quarters was still loss-making, and the ~120-140x trailing PE is pricing in unconfirmed pipeline optionality rather than demonstrated earnings power. The quant model's own 3-year window score also lands on Sell; we are not persuaded the valuation gap is closed enough to rescue to Hold.
summary: Wockhardt has genuinely turned around operationally -- from a loss in FY25 to a Rs 199 Cr profit in FY26 with improving margins each quarter -- and carries a long-standing, differentiated pipeline in novel antibiotics that could be a meaningful longer-term value driver if it converts to approved, marketed products. At the current price, however, the stock already trades at more than 100 times trailing earnings, a multiple the underlying return on equity (~6%) does not yet support, and quarterly results have been volatile (a loss as recently as June 2025). We would treat this as a Sell for portfolio purposes on valuation grounds, notwithstanding the improving underlying trend.
positive_para: Revenue grew 12% in FY26 with margins expanding in every quarter (13% to 19% OPM), turning a Rs 57 Cr loss into a Rs 199 Cr profit -- a real, not merely accounting, improvement. Debt is modest and interest burden is declining. The company's long-running R&D program in novel gram-negative antibiotics remains a differentiated, hard-to-replicate franchise relative to the largely generic Indian pharma peer set, offering optionality beyond the base business.
negative_para: Three-year ROE of ~6% and ROCE of ~8% are both low, and one of the last four quarters (June 2025) was still a loss -- this is not yet a stable, de-risked earnings stream. At 120-140x trailing earnings the market has already priced in a great deal of future success, most plausibly tied to the antibiotic pipeline, but we found no confirmed evidence in the sources reviewed of near-term revenue contribution from that pipeline; if it slips, the stock has very little valuation support from the base generics/API business alone. Promoter holding has more than halved since 2017.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 120-140x trailing multiple against ~6% ROE and ~12% revenue growth requires either a step-change in earnings (most plausibly a pipeline monetization event) that is not yet visible in reported numbers, or several more years of the current margin-recovery trend compounding -- neither is underwritable today. We read this as rich relative to demonstrated fundamentals.
